fixes.explanation: Scattered? Nobody gets scattered here, baker. The text says many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized (Acts 18:8). I think that's the happiest line in the whole passage, so I'm not letting anyone scatter it. The trouble waits for us later.

Nobody's fighting over the synagogue keys here, friend. Gallio calls it “…a dispute about words and names and your own law…” (Acts 18:15). I think the keys were safe the whole time. He just wants no part of it, and he sends them off to settle it themselves.

Land? Nobody's fighting about land, baker. Gallio calls it “…a dispute about words and names and your own law…” (Acts 18:15). I bet he'd have been just as done with a land fight, because he tells them to settle it themselves. He says he refuses to be a judge of such things.
